findings: The command-log extension reuses the existing token-aware primitive scanner instead of adding a second detector.
CI scans a deterministic repo-tracked redacted corpus and remains independent of raw local agent logs.
Regression tests cover direct git, nested shell command, cmd field, JSON-encoded arguments, tool-only missing surface, and unredacted records.
Operators use one gate command with --require-command-log-corpus and receive record counts in output.
Targeted tests, clippy, command corpus gate, quality/protection/aspirational/planning gates, JSON parsing, and diff hygiene passed.

alternatives_named: Scan raw session logs in CI
Use curated redacted repo-tracked command corpus
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Curated redacted corpus is CI-safe and enforceable now without leaking local session data.

findings: Records without redacted=true are rejected and raw local logs are out of default scan scope.
Corpus parsing is linear over JSONL records; current corpus checks 3 records.
Evidence explicitly limits claims to sanitized tracked corpus and hosted verification gap.
Reversible by removing the corpus flag/wiring and registry corpus file; no data migration.
Gate output includes command-log record counts plus source/fence/usage counts.

F12_reserved.not_applicable_reason: No active F12 requirement in current spec.

findings: P17 historical lane now points to the active command-log aware successor command.
New paths use existing evidence and registry naming conventions.
Fitness lane docs, CI-lane docs, and plan surfaces now name the command corpus requirement.
Kernel remains pure; dev-cli owns JSONL/file loading.
No filesystem/env access added to the kernel.

The original assumption that the blocker required raw session-log ingestion was narrowed: CI-safe enforcement can start with curated redacted command-log corpus, while raw historical completeness remains a non-claim.
The change fits the FD-001 pipeline as a serialized governance gate that enables safer later fanout without reading private local logs or bypassing Oya VCS policy.

non_claims: Does not read raw .audit, .omx, home-directory transcripts, shell histories, or unstaged local session logs in CI.
Does not prove the hosted GitHub branch-protection ruleset was deployed or that a remote Actions run has completed on this branch.
Does not claim historical tool-call completeness beyond the curated sanitized corpus checked into the repository.
Does not close dependency-seam, OpenAPI binding, API-before-handler, data-ownership, or other FD-001 product fanout blockers.
remaining_blockers: Hosted GitHub Actions run and branch-protection deployment still require a GitOps/admin verification lane before hosted enforcement can be claimed.
Raw local/session transcript ingestion remains intentionally out of CI scope; future evidence would need a redaction/export adapter before expanding beyond curated tracked corpus.
FD-001 product/API/data fanout remains blocked until the next serialized shared-gate lanes are reconciled.
